::: {.lede}
Two connected strands: modelling the behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics,
and evaluating whether the interventions built on them are cost-effective.
:::

## Interests

- Infectious disease modelling
- Epidemiological modelling
- Machine learning
- Health economics
- Cost-utility modelling
- Economic evaluation

## Projects

### Behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics

The doctoral project. Social contact, mobility and attitude data carry signal
about how people actually behave during an outbreak — who mixes with whom, how
that changes under pressure, and how quickly it reverts. The question is whether
that signal can be used not just to explain epidemic dynamics after the fact,
but to forecast them.

### Economic evaluation of blood-borne virus screening

NIHR-funded work on whether blood-borne virus testing interventions are worth
what they cost: coding hepatitis B progression models to evaluate emergency
department opt-out testing, assessing TB IGRA testing in high-risk groups, and
micro-costing digitally enhanced BBV testing.

### Vaccine responses and vaccine equity

Earlier work using machine learning to understand vaccine responses to
influenza, and modelling vaccine equity and trachoma resurgence.
